clue.text: What Cortes organised to protect himself

definitions.text: What Cortes organised to protect himself

indicators.note: organised means the six letters of the conquistador's name are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: The Spanish conquistador arranges his own bodyguard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges CORTES; the whole clue also describes a guard, which is what Cortes would arrange to keep himself safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodyguard accompanying someone for protection is a protective companion of that kind.

clue.text: Monstrousness in crime or in enmity

indicators.note: in crime treats the letters as acting criminally, that is, out of their lawful order

explanation.surface: Wickedness is found both in criminal acts and in hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in crime' rearranges OR and ENMITY; the second 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme wickedness or outrageousness is this sense of the word.

clue.text: About a hundred years needed for a pharmaceutical plant

indicators.note: About means one piece goes round another

parts.note: a century is a hundred years

explanation.surface: A medicinal herb takes about a hundred years to develop.
explanation.definitionFit: A small gentian-family herb used in herbal medicine.

clue.text: Ceremony pronounced as fit and proper

indicators.note: pronounced tells us the word is said out loud rather than spelt

explanation.surface: A ritual is declared to be appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal religious or solemn ritual.

clue.text: Invite trouble in the hope of getting a pay rise?

definitions.text: in the hope of getting a pay rise?

explanation.surface: A worker wonders whether demanding more money will only bring problems.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke trouble is the idiom 'be asking for it'; literally, one requests the rise to get it.

clue.text: Maybe set one's feet astride and keep up

explanation.surface: Someone braces themselves, legs apart, and manages to stay with the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, planting the feet a stride apart; idiomatically, coping with the speed of others.

clue.text: Sack from shoot

explanation.surface: Someone is dismissed from a photo session.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss from a job; to discharge a gun.

clue.text: Bacon's cut is bolder

explanation.surface: A slice from the philosopher Bacon is more daring.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice of cured pork; more reckless, as the comparative of hasty.

clue.text: Bound to have a prior engagement

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to have another appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastened with rope; busy and so unavailable.

clue.text: Highly decorative or neat design

indicators.note: design here signals that the letters are laid out in a new pattern

explanation.surface: A choice between something elaborately ornamented or something tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamented and elaborate in style, the opposite of plain.

clue.text: Jersey is a poetically beautiful sea-girt land

parts.note: fair is the poetic word for beautiful
an isle is a piece of land surrounded by sea

explanation.surface: Jersey, the Channel Island, is praised as a lovely island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' suggests the Channel Island but means a knitted sweater, named after a Shetland island famous for its patterned knitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fair Isle is a sweater knitted in a multicoloured Shetland pattern, and a jersey is a sweater.

clue.text: Cause ill feeling-that is what deficient marrow cells do

explanation.surface: Faulty bone marrow is blamed for bad feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To create resentment is the idiom; literally, defective marrow produces faulty red cells.

clue.text: Atom splitting is an outmoded form of defence

indicators.note: splitting the atom breaks the word into pieces to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Nuclear fission has made older forms of defence obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-filled ditch round a castle was a medieval protection no longer used.

clue.text: Father is divine during the whole 24 hours

indicators.note: during means one piece falls within the span of the other

parts.note: a full day is twenty-four hours
a divine is a clergyman, and DD (Doctor of Divinity) stands for one

explanation.surface: A priest is called Father around the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's priest called Father misleads: 'divine' gives letters, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Daddy is a child's familiar word for a dad.

clue.text: Pizarro left part of its hope ruined

indicators.note: part of shows the letters are a stretch lying within the following words

explanation.surface: The conquistador left a land whose hopes were in ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across hoPE RUined. Pizarro conquered the Inca empire and left it devastated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish conquistador Pizarro conquered the South American Inca land and left it in ruins.

clue.text: Works I lost in chaotic circumstances

indicators.note: chaotic says the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Something gets lost amid disorder at the factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Labours hard, as a verb meaning to slog away.

clue.text: New names for ministerial accommodation

indicators.note: New tells us the letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Fresh names are given to clergy housing.
explanation.definitionFit: A house provided for a Scottish Presbyterian or other minister.

clue.text: Look around for a girl to infatuate you

definitions.text: for a girl to infatuate you

explanation.surface: A man glances round as a pretty girl walks past.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance behind you is literally to rotate the neck; to have your judgement swept away by someone is the idiom for being smitten.

clue.text: Visited with a request to serve

explanation.surface: Someone drops by asking for help.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid a visit to; summoned to perform a duty.

clue.text: Uninspired — by the living facilities presumably

explanation.surface: Someone feels dull beside the housing.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling deflated is one sense; literally, it is a position to the side of an apartment.

clue.text: Mine sweeper's mission easily understood by readers

explanation.surface: A minesweeper's task is described alongside a readable piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A minesweeper aims to open a safe route through the water; a lucid piece of text is also a transparent extract.

clue.text: Turn up unannounced and somewhat drunk

explanation.surface: A guest arrives without warning, rather tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: To call casually is one sense; having a small drink inside you is the other.

clue.text: Aspire in order to gain what the Shah lost

indicators.note: in order to gain asks the letters to be put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Ambitious people aspire to regain what the Shah forfeited.
explanation.walkthrough: The last Shah of Iran, the country once called this, lost his throne in 1979.
explanation.definitionFit: The old name of Iran, the kingdom the Shah ruled until the revolution.

clue.text: Shorten sail if heeling towards it

explanation.surface: A sailor takes in canvas as the boat leans towards danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce canvas area is to tie in a sail; a ship heeling towards a rocky ridge under water is in peril.

clue.text: How a shocked man is taken to be a footballer

definitions.text: How a shocked man is taken

parts.note: a back is a defensive footballer

explanation.surface: A man is startled to be mistaken for a football player.
explanation.definitionFit: Being startled is the idiom 'taken aback', so the word completes the phrase.

clue.text: Regular TV appearance provides an opening for Penny

explanation.surface: A television regular is given a chance by someone called Penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheduled broadcast time is a regular spot; a coin is put into the narrow aperture of a vending machine.

clue.text: Let's reform, just in case

indicators.note: reform means the letters are shaped anew

explanation.surface: A call to reform, just to be safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjunction meaning to avoid the risk that, a precaution.

clue.text: Thanks again, and good-bye

indicators.note: again means the same word is given a second time

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Saying thanks once more on parting.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual British farewell, a synonym of cheerio.

clue.text: Forced to board, but persevered.

explanation.surface: A passenger is shoved onto a vehicle yet keeps going.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoved aboard is one sense; carried on doggedly is the phrasal verb's other sense.

clue.text: Bach and Elgar central to another composer

indicators.note: central means the wanted letters sit in the middle of the following phrase

explanation.surface: Two composers are said to be key to a third.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside bacH AND ELgar.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was a Baroque composer of Messiah.

clue.text: When the water churned ain't deep

indicators.note: churned water is stirred up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Stirred-up water turns out to be shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churned' rearranges AINTDEEP. A neap tide is the time of month when the water rises least, hence 'ain't deep'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide of minimal range is a time describing the state of the sea, so it says when the water is low.

clue.text: Is it meant to catch motorists who cross the frontier without it?

definitions.text: Is it meant to catch motorists who cross the frontier without it?

parts.words: Is it meant to catch motorists who cross the frontier without it?
parts.note: read as a car-catching net it sounds like a trap, but it is the customs permit drivers need at a border

explanation.surface: A trap seems set for drivers crossing the border without papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A customs permit allowing a vehicle to be taken temporarily across borders.
